title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to curb excessive charging for AI services and prevent employers from fixing or suppressing wages in the AI industry. It establishes rules for price transparency and worker protections to ensure fair compensation and prevent market manipulation.

title: BRIDGE AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The BRIDGE AI Act is a proposed law that seeks to create a unified framework bridging gaps between current AI regulations and emerging technologies, promoting responsible development and deployment. It emphasizes transparency, accountability, and safety while encouraging innovation and protecting public interests.

title: Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The policy outlines a comprehensive plan to protect public health from the risks and challenges posed by artificial intelligence. It sets out steps for identifying, assessing, and mitigating AI‑driven threats through collaboration, regulation, and ongoing monitoring.

title: A bill to require the Securities and Exchange Commission to issue rules relating to the use of artificial intelligence by public companies, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: This bill directs the Securities and Exchange Commission to create regulations that govern how public companies can use artificial intelligence. It also includes additional provisions related to the broader oversight of AI in the public market.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes regulations to ensure that AI research and development are conducted in a trustworthy, safe, and accountable manner. It mandates rigorous testing, transparency, and oversight for AI systems to promote reliability and mitigate potential risks.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through CISA, to set up a pilot program that uses AI to defend critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It also includes additional related provisions that are not detailed in the available text.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act would create a task force dedicated to addressing cybersecurity risks posed by artificial‑intelligence systems. Its goal is to bring federal agencies together, set safety standards, and protect critical infrastructure from AI‑related cyber threats.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed regulation aimed at governing the development and use of artificial intelligence. It seeks to establish safety standards, accountability mechanisms, and ethical guidelines to ensure that AI systems are transparent, fair, and aligned with societal values.

title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 seeks to stop companies from using software that secretly coordinates prices or other market actions, thereby protecting competition. It establishes rules and penalties that make it easier for regulators to detect and punish any algorithm‑driven collusion among firms.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to help small businesses access and implement AI technology by providing training resources and funding. It seeks to ensure small enterprises can develop and use AI safely and competitively in the marketplace.

title: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency the National Cyber and AI Investigations Board to investigate significant cyber incidents, cyber incidents involving terrorism, and cyber incidents involving artificial intelligence, to determine root causes and develop recommendations to prevent similar incidents and address terrorism threats to the United States, including threats relating to the malicious use of information systems or artificial intelligence by covered foreign adversaries, including terrorist organizations, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This amendment to the Homeland Security Act establishes a National Cyber and AI Investigations Board within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. The board will investigate major cyber incidents, including those involving terrorism or AI, identify root causes, and recommend ways to prevent future threats from foreign adversaries and terrorist groups.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act temporarily stops the building or expanding of new data centers specifically for AI, aiming to address environmental, regulatory, and societal concerns. The pause gives lawmakers and stakeholders time to develop guidelines and evaluate the long‑term impacts before AI infrastructure can resume growth.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes a framework for assessing the environmental footprint of AI systems, including energy use, carbon emissions, and electronic waste. It requires AI developers and users to report key metrics, adopt mitigation strategies, and invest in greener technologies to minimize overall ecological impact.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes legal requirements for measuring and reducing the environmental footprint of AI technologies. It sets standards for energy use, carbon emissions, and data center efficiency, and creates a reporting framework for companies deploying AI systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on building or operating new AI data centers. It aims to give lawmakers time to assess the environmental, energy, and social impacts of these facilities before allowing them to expand.

title: American AI Security Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American AI Security Act is a proposed law that seeks to create a comprehensive regulatory framework for the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence to safeguard national security and public safety. It would set standards for transparency, accountability, and risk assessment of AI systems and establish enforcement mechanisms to address potential threats and misuse.

title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that requires the government to oversee and regulate artificial‑intelligence technologies in specific high‑risk industries, such as healthcare, finance, and transportation. It establishes industry‑specific rules, safety standards, and accountability measures to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with public interests.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says Congress should not give extra money or special regulatory help to companies or banks that are at risk of collapse because of stress in the artificial‑intelligence market. Instead, the House urges Congress to direct support toward all Americans who have been harmed.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act is a legislative framework designed to regulate the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence within the VET sector. It sets out standards for transparency, safety, accountability, and ethical considerations to protect users and ensure responsible AI practices.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 bans the use of artificial intelligence for diagnosing or treating patients, insisting that all medical decisions be made by licensed human doctors. It also mandates strict licensing and oversight to keep patient care safe and accountable.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 is a law that requires companies using AI and other automated systems to evaluate and mitigate risks such as bias, privacy violations, and safety hazards. It establishes regulatory oversight and reporting obligations so that developers and users must demonstrate how their algorithms operate fairly, transparently, and responsibly.
